# images.types: TiledImage

Copied from source, comments included. A comment records intent. The body is the algorithm. Neither is a proof that the result is correct. Names resolve in the whole compilation.

This slice: TiledImage, AnimatedImage, ImageRegion, VolumeImage, CubemapImage.

```plato

// A large image split into a row-major grid of tiles for streaming and
// caching. Interior tiles are exactly TileSize; right/bottom edge tiles may
// be smaller.
type TiledImage
    implements IValue
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    TileSize: IntegerSize2D;
    Tiles: Array<FloatImage>;
}

// A frame-sequence image (animated GIF/WebP style). FrameDurations pairs
// one-to-one with Frames; LoopCount is the replay count, 0 meaning forever.
type AnimatedImage
    implements IValue
{
    Frames: Array<Bitmap>;
    FrameDurations: Array<Duration>;
    LoopCount: Integer;
}

// A rectangular region of interest within an image, in pixel coordinates.
// Contains Min, excludes Max (half-open, like IntegerBounds2D).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region_of_interest)
type ImageRegion
    implements IValue
{
    Bounds: IntegerBounds2D;
}

//==
// ## Volume and cubemap pixel data

// A dense 3D scalar grid (a voxel image): medical stacks, density fields
// baked to texels, 3D noise caches. Values are layer-major: layer, then row,
// then column; Count equals Width times Height times Depth.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voxel)
type VolumeImage
    implements IValue
{
    Size: IntegerSize3D;
    Values: Array<Number>;
}

// The six square faces of a cubemap as linear-light images, in the order
// +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z. All faces share the same square size.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cube_mapping)
type CubemapImage
    implements IValue
{
    Faces: Array<FloatImage>;
}
```
